title: Universal enhancement of the pairing gap in a dilute Fermi superfluid
authors: Silas R. Beane, Roland C. Farrell, Cameron P. Shotwell
abstract: At zero temperature, a dilute Fermi gas with an attractive contact interaction forms a superfluid with gapped fermionic excitations. We show that the gap at weak coupling can be organized as a trans-series expansion in the interaction strength and the asymptotic Gor'kov-Melik-Barkhudarov gap. Low-energy virtual quasiparticles generate corrections that are linear in the gap with a leading coefficient nearly 25$\times$ larger than the other known coefficients. This substantially increases the gap at intermediate densities, highlighting that systematic corrections are crucial for quantitative predictions.
summary: This theoretical paper calculates the pairing gap in a dilute Fermi superfluid using a systematic trans-series expansion method. By including higher-order quantum corrections, the authors predict a substantial enhancement of the gap, which is crucial for accurate quantitative predictions in ultracold atomic systems. The methodology involves advanced diagrammatic techniques applied to the gap equation.
main_problem: The paper aims to determine the pairing gap in a dilute Fermi superfluid by systematically calculating higher-order corrections to the gap equation.
main_result: The pairing gap is found to be a trans-series expansion, with a specific correction term showing a leading coefficient nearly 25 times larger than previously known coefficients.
method: The authors employ a systematic, diagrammatic weak-coupling expansion of the gap equation derived from the Goldstone pole condition, calculating coefficients order-by-order.
model_or_system: The system is a spin-1/2 Fermi gas interacting via a short-range attractive contact interaction. The analysis uses the gap equation derived from the pairing correlator, treating the gap as a trans-series in the interaction strength and the asymptotic gap.
key_observables: Pairing gap ($\Delta$), dimensionless quantities ($\lambda$, $x$), and the trans-series coefficients ($c_{n,m}$).
important_parameters: Interaction strength ($g_0$), Fermi momentum ($k_F$), and the density regime (intermediate densities).
main_assumptions: The calculation relies on diagrammatic perturbation theory and involves approximations when evaluating complex integrals in different momentum regimes.
figures_summary: Figures compare the calculated trans-series prediction for the gap against results from the GMB theory, Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations, and experimental data from ultracold atoms.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the gap equation via the pole condition, deriving the trans-series expansion coefficients through successive orders of approximation ($R[1], R[2], R[3]$), and finally evaluating complex integrals to obtain closed-form expressions for the gap enhancement.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly quantitative, systematic theoretical framework for calculating superfluid properties in ultracold atomic gases, directly addressing the need for high-precision predictions beyond mean-field theory.

The integration region that generates the linear-in-∆ term in the irreducible pairing potential is the intersection of two spherical shells, each with radius kF and thickness proportional to ∆/kF . a) For zero thickness and sphere sep- aration 0 < |q| < 2kF , the intersection is a ring with O(kF ) radius. b) Adding in the thickness, the intersection volume has a toroidal shape with cross-sectional area O(∆2/k2 F ) and volume O(∆2/kF ).

FIG. 3. The solid blue line is the superfluid gap predicted from the weak coupling expansion including the c1,0 and c2,1 corrections to GMB. It is compared to GMB (dashed gray line), QMC with an effective range |re/a| ≈0.15 [31] (orange) and ultracold atom experiment [32] (green). The shaded blue region is a 68% uncertainty band on the trans-series predic- tion.
